name: P1 · Computer Literacy
description: 4 of 14 topics so far (8 sets × 20 questions): Unit 1 – Introduction to Computer; Unit 2 – Operating Systems; Unit 2 – Window Settings & Advanced Windows; Unit 3 – MS Office (Word). More topics are added to this pack as the plan goes on; re-importing only adds the new sets.

sets.name: 1 · What is a Computer, Categories and Types

questions.question: A computer is best described as an electronic device that:

options.A: Accepts data, processes it according to instructions, stores it and produces output
options.D: Thinks and decides on its own without instructions

questions.subject: What is a Computer, Categories and Types
questions.explanation: Input → process → output, with storage, all under program control.

questions.question: The word 'computer' is derived from the word 'compute', which means:
questions.subject: What is a Computer, Categories and Types
questions.explanation: Early computers were built mainly for calculation.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a characteristic of a computer?

options.D: It has its own intelligence (IQ) and feelings

questions.subject: What is a Computer, Categories and Types
questions.explanation: A computer has zero IQ; it only follows the instructions given to it.

questions.question: The principle GIGO means:

options.B: Garbage In, Garbage Out – wrong input or instructions give wrong output
options.D: Good Input, Good Output – the computer corrects errors

questions.subject: What is a Computer, Categories and Types
questions.explanation: Computer errors are mostly caused by wrong data or wrong programs.

questions.question: On the basis of how they work (the type of data they handle), computers are classified as:
questions.subject: What is a Computer, Categories and Types
questions.explanation: Size gives micro/mini/mainframe/super; purpose gives general/special.

questions.question: A car's speedometer showing speed by a moving needle is an example of an:
questions.subject: What is a Computer, Categories and Types
questions.explanation: It measures a continuously changing quantity.

questions.question: A machine in a hospital ICU that measures a patient's heartbeat and blood pressure (analog) and displays them as numbers (digital) is an example of a:
questions.subject: What is a Computer, Categories and Types
questions.explanation: Hybrid computers combine analog measurement with digital processing.

questions.question: Arrange computers by size and computing power, from smallest to largest:
questions.subject: What is a Computer, Categories and Types
questions.explanation: Supercomputers are the fastest and most powerful.

questions.question: PARAM, India's first supercomputer series, was developed by:
questions.subject: What is a Computer, Categories and Types
questions.explanation: PARAM 8000 was released in 1991.

questions.question: The speed of supercomputers is usually measured in:
questions.subject: What is a Computer, Categories and Types
questions.explanation: Modern supercomputers work in petaFLOPS and exaFLOPS.

questions.question: Large organisations such as banks and railway reservation systems, which support thousands of users at the same time, mainly use:
questions.subject: What is a Computer, Categories and Types
questions.explanation: Mainframes handle huge volumes of transactions reliably.

questions.question: A computer built into a washing machine to control its washing cycle is called:
questions.subject: What is a Computer, Categories and Types
questions.explanation: Embedded systems are special-purpose computers inside other devices.

questions.question: Desktop PCs, laptops, tablets and smartphones are all examples of:
questions.subject: What is a Computer, Categories and Types
questions.explanation: They are built around a microprocessor and are used by one person at a time.

questions.question: A computer that provides files, web pages or other services to other computers on a network is called a:
questions.subject: What is a Computer, Categories and Types
questions.explanation: Clients request services; servers provide them.

questions.question:
Match the computer with a typical use:
a. Supercomputer
b. Mainframe
c. Microcomputer
d. Embedded computer

1. Bank transaction processing
2. Controlling a microwave oven
3. Personal work at home or office
4. Weather forecasting
questions.subject: What is a Computer, Categories and Types
questions.explanation: Weather forecasting needs the huge speed of supercomputers.

questions.question:
Consider the statements:
I. A general-purpose computer can run many different kinds of programs.
II. A special-purpose computer is designed for one particular task.
Which is/are correct?
questions.subject: What is a Computer, Categories and Types
questions.explanation: E.g. a PC is general-purpose; a traffic-signal controller is special-purpose.

questions.question:
Consider the statements:
I. Digital computers work with discrete values (digits).
II. Analog computers are more accurate than digital computers.
Which is/are correct?
questions.subject: What is a Computer, Categories and Types
questions.explanation: Digital computers are more accurate; analog ones work with continuous quantities.

questions.question:
Assertion (A): Computers can work for long hours without loss of accuracy.
Reason (R): Computers do not suffer from tiredness or lack of concentration.

options.A: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
options.B: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
options.C: A is true, but R is false
options.D: A is false, but R is true

questions.subject: What is a Computer, Categories and Types
questions.explanation: This quality is called diligence.

questions.question:
Assertion (A): A computer can decide by itself what problem to solve.
Reason (R): A computer works only according to the instructions given in a program.

options.A: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
options.B: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
options.C: A is true, but R is false
options.D: A is false, but R is true

questions.subject: What is a Computer, Categories and Types
questions.explanation: Because it only follows programs, it cannot decide by itself; R shows why A is false.

questions.question:
Assertion (A): Supercomputers are used for weather forecasting.
Reason (R): Supercomputers are the smallest and cheapest computers.

options.A: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
options.B: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
options.C: A is true, but R is false
options.D: A is false, but R is true

questions.subject: What is a Computer, Categories and Types
questions.explanation: A is true because forecasting needs enormous calculation; R is false – they are the largest and costliest.

sets.name: 2 · Languages, Applications, Memory, Hardware and Software

questions.question: The only language a computer can execute directly, written in 0s and 1s, is:
questions.subject: Languages, Applications, Memory, Hardware and Software
questions.explanation: All other languages must be translated into machine language.

questions.question: Assembly language uses:

options.A: Mnemonics (short codes) such as ADD and MOV

questions.subject: Languages, Applications, Memory, Hardware and Software
questions.explanation: An assembler translates it into machine code.

questions.question:
Match the translator with its job:
a. Compiler
b. Interpreter
c. Assembler

1. Translates and executes a high-level program line by line
2. Translates a whole high-level program at once
3. Translates assembly language to machine code
questions.subject: Languages, Applications, Memory, Hardware and Software
questions.explanation: Compilers produce a complete object program; interpreters do not.

questions.question: Which of the following is a high-level language?
questions.subject: Languages, Applications, Memory, Hardware and Software
questions.explanation: High-level languages are close to human language and machine-independent.

questions.question: 1 kilobyte (KB) is equal to:
questions.subject: Languages, Applications, Memory, Hardware and Software
questions.explanation: 2¹⁰ = 1024; 1 byte = 8 bits.

questions.question: Half a byte (4 bits) is called a:
questions.subject: Languages, Applications, Memory, Hardware and Software
questions.explanation: A byte has two nibbles.

questions.question: Arrange in increasing order of size:
questions.subject: Languages, Applications, Memory, Hardware and Software
questions.explanation: Each unit is 1024 times the previous one.

questions.question: Which memory loses its contents when the power is switched off?
questions.subject: Languages, Applications, Memory, Hardware and Software
questions.explanation: RAM is volatile; the others keep data without power.

questions.question: The BIOS program that starts a computer is usually stored in:
questions.subject: Languages, Applications, Memory, Hardware and Software
questions.explanation: Software permanently stored in ROM chips is called firmware.

questions.question: Arrange in order from fastest to slowest:

options.B: CPU registers, cache memory, RAM, hard disk

questions.subject: Languages, Applications, Memory, Hardware and Software
questions.explanation: Faster memory is smaller and costlier per byte.

questions.question: A standard single-layer DVD can store about:
questions.subject: Languages, Applications, Memory, Hardware and Software
questions.explanation: A CD holds about 700 MB and a single-layer Blu-ray about 25 GB.

questions.question: Which of these is secondary (auxiliary) storage?
questions.subject: Languages, Applications, Memory, Hardware and Software
questions.explanation: Secondary storage is non-volatile and holds data permanently.

questions.question: Intel and AMD are well-known manufacturers of:
questions.subject: Languages, Applications, Memory, Hardware and Software
questions.explanation: Dell, HP and Lenovo make complete computers; Microsoft makes Windows.

questions.question:
Match the software with its type:
a. Windows
b. MS Word
c. Antivirus program
d. Device driver

1. Operating system (system software)
2. Utility software
3. Application software
4. Software that lets the OS control a hardware device
questions.subject: Languages, Applications, Memory, Hardware and Software
questions.explanation: Operating systems and drivers are system software.

questions.question: Software whose source code is freely available to be studied, changed and shared, such as Linux, is called:
questions.subject: Languages, Applications, Memory, Hardware and Software
questions.explanation: Windows and MS Office are proprietary (closed-source).

questions.question: Software that can be used free for a trial period, after which the user is asked to pay, is called:
questions.subject: Languages, Applications, Memory, Hardware and Software
questions.explanation: Freeware is free to use without payment.

questions.question:
Consider the statements:
I. Hardware refers to the physical parts of a computer.
II. Software can work without any hardware.
Which is/are correct?
questions.subject: Languages, Applications, Memory, Hardware and Software
questions.explanation: Hardware and software need each other: software runs on hardware.

questions.question:
Consider the statements:
I. ATMs and online banking are applications of computers in banking.
II. E-governance uses computers to deliver government services to citizens.
Which is/are correct?
questions.subject: Languages, Applications, Memory, Hardware and Software
questions.explanation: Both are common applications of computers.

questions.question:
Assertion (A): Programs written in a high-level language must be translated before execution.
Reason (R): A computer can directly execute only machine language.

options.A: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
options.B: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
options.C: A is true, but R is false
options.D: A is false, but R is true

questions.subject: Languages, Applications, Memory, Hardware and Software
questions.explanation: Compilers or interpreters convert them into machine code.

questions.question:
Assertion (A): RAM is used to store data permanently.
Reason (R): RAM is volatile memory.

options.A: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
options.B: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
options.C: A is true, but R is false
options.D: A is false, but R is true

questions.subject: Languages, Applications, Memory, Hardware and Software
questions.explanation: Because RAM is volatile, it cannot store data permanently; R shows why A is false.

sets.name: 1 · Operating System: Meaning, Functions and Types

questions.question: An operating system is best described as:

options.B: System software that manages the computer's hardware and resources and acts as an interface between the user and the hardware
options.C: A hardware device inside the CPU

questions.subject: Operating System: Meaning, Functions and Types
questions.explanation: Without an OS, users and application programs could not use the hardware easily.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a function of an operating system?
questions.subject: Operating System: Meaning, Functions and Types
questions.explanation: Typing letters is done by application software such as a word processor.

questions.question: The core part of an operating system that stays in memory and directly controls the hardware is the:
questions.subject: Operating System: Meaning, Functions and Types
questions.explanation: The shell (command line or GUI) is the part that interacts with the user.

questions.question: The Linux kernel was first released in 1991 by:
questions.subject: Operating System: Meaning, Functions and Types
questions.explanation: Linux is free and open-source.

questions.question: Red Hat is best known as:

options.C: A company that develops and supports a distribution of Linux (Red Hat Enterprise Linux)

questions.subject: Operating System: Meaning, Functions and Types
questions.explanation: Other Linux distributions include Ubuntu, Debian and Fedora.

questions.question: The operating system used on Apple's Macintosh computers is:
questions.subject: Operating System: Meaning, Functions and Types
questions.explanation: It was earlier called Mac OS X / OS X.

questions.question: Windows is developed by:
questions.subject: Operating System: Meaning, Functions and Types
questions.explanation: Windows 1.0 was released in 1985.

questions.question: MS-DOS differs from Windows mainly because MS-DOS has a:

options.D: Command-line interface where commands are typed

questions.subject: Operating System: Meaning, Functions and Types
questions.explanation: Windows provides a GUI with windows, icons, menus and a pointer.

questions.question: An operating system that must respond to inputs within strict time limits, such as in air-traffic control or medical equipment, is a:
questions.subject: Operating System: Meaning, Functions and Types
questions.explanation: Missing a deadline in such systems can be dangerous.

questions.question: In a batch operating system:

options.A: Similar jobs are collected and run one after another without user interaction
options.B: Many users interact with the computer at the same time
options.C: Each job must respond in real time

questions.subject: Operating System: Meaning, Functions and Types
questions.explanation: It was common in early mainframe computing.

questions.question: An operating system that allows several users to work on one computer at the same time, each through a terminal, is:
questions.subject: Operating System: Meaning, Functions and Types
questions.explanation: UNIX and Linux are multi-user operating systems.

questions.question: Android, the mobile operating system, is based on the:
questions.subject: Operating System: Meaning, Functions and Types
questions.explanation: Android is developed by Google.

questions.question: Loading the operating system into main memory when the computer is switched on is called:
questions.subject: Operating System: Meaning, Functions and Types
questions.explanation: A cold boot starts from power-off; a warm boot is a restart.

questions.question: The program that starts first when a PC is switched on and begins the boot process is stored in:

options.A: A text file on the desktop
options.C: BIOS/UEFI firmware on a ROM chip

questions.subject: Operating System: Meaning, Functions and Types
questions.explanation: It tests the hardware (POST) and then loads the OS.

questions.question: Restarting a computer that is already on, without switching off the power, is called a:
questions.subject: Operating System: Meaning, Functions and Types
questions.explanation: Switching on from a powered-off state is a cold boot.

questions.question:
Match the operating system with its developer:
a. Windows
b. macOS
c. Android
d. Red Hat Enterprise Linux

1. Microsoft
2. Google
3. Apple
4. Red Hat
questions.subject: Operating System: Meaning, Functions and Types
questions.explanation: iOS (for iPhones) is also developed by Apple.

questions.question:
Consider the statements:
I. Linux is open-source software.
II. Windows is open-source software.
Which is/are correct?
questions.subject: Operating System: Meaning, Functions and Types
questions.explanation: Windows and macOS are proprietary; their source code is not freely available.

questions.question:
Consider the statements:
I. The operating system manages memory and files.
II. The operating system provides the user interface.
Which is/are correct?
questions.subject: Operating System: Meaning, Functions and Types
questions.explanation: Both are standard functions of an operating system.

questions.question:
Assertion (A): A computer cannot be used conveniently without an operating system.
Reason (R): The operating system manages the hardware and provides an interface for users and programs.

options.A: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
options.B: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
options.C: A is true, but R is false
options.D: A is false, but R is true

questions.subject: Operating System: Meaning, Functions and Types
questions.explanation: The OS is the link between users, programs and hardware.

questions.question:
Assertion (A): MS Word is an operating system.
Reason (R): An operating system manages the computer's hardware resources.

options.A: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
options.B: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
options.C: A is true, but R is false
options.D: A is false, but R is true

questions.subject: Operating System: Meaning, Functions and Types
questions.explanation: MS Word is application software, since it does not manage hardware; R shows why A is false.

questions.question: The four main elements of a graphical user interface are summarised as WIMP, which stands for:
questions.subject: Windows Concepts, Mouse and Icons
questions.explanation: Windows introduced a WIMP-style GUI for PCs.

questions.question: The strip, usually at the bottom of the Windows screen, that holds the Start button, open programs and the clock is the:
questions.subject: Windows Concepts, Mouse and Icons
questions.explanation: The area near the clock is the notification area (system tray).

questions.question: A small picture on the desktop that represents a program, file or folder is called an:
questions.subject: Windows Concepts, Mouse and Icons
questions.explanation: Double-clicking an icon opens the item.

questions.question: A desktop icon with a small curved arrow at its lower-left corner is a:

options.B: Shortcut to a file, folder or program

questions.subject: Windows Concepts, Mouse and Icons
questions.explanation: Deleting a shortcut does not delete the original item.

questions.question: Files deleted from the hard disk in Windows normally go first to the:

options.C: Recycle Bin, from where they can be restored

questions.subject: Windows Concepts, Mouse and Icons
questions.explanation: They are removed permanently only when the Recycle Bin is emptied.

questions.question: Pressing Shift + Delete on a selected file in Windows:

options.D: Deletes it permanently without sending it to the Recycle Bin

questions.subject: Windows Concepts, Mouse and Icons
questions.explanation: Windows usually asks for confirmation first.

questions.question:
Match the mouse action with its usual result:
a. Single click
b. Double click
c. Right click
d. Drag and drop

1. Moves an item to a new place
2. Opens a file or program
3. Opens a context (shortcut) menu
4. Selects an item
questions.subject: Windows Concepts, Mouse and Icons
questions.explanation: These are the basic mouse operations in Windows.

questions.question: To move an icon to another place on the desktop, the user should:

options.A: Drag it with the left mouse button held down and release it at the new place

questions.subject: Windows Concepts, Mouse and Icons
questions.explanation: If 'Auto arrange icons' is on, Windows arranges them automatically.

questions.question: The three buttons at the right end of a window's title bar are:
questions.subject: Windows Concepts, Mouse and Icons
questions.explanation: A minimised window stays available on the taskbar.

questions.question: Which keyboard shortcut switches between open windows in Windows?
questions.subject: Windows Concepts, Mouse and Icons
questions.explanation: Alt + F4 closes the active window.

questions.question:
Match the Windows shortcut with its action:
a. Windows key + D
b. Windows key + E
c. Windows key + L
d. Alt + F4

1. Open File Explorer
2. Close the active window
3. Lock the computer
4. Show the desktop
questions.subject: Windows Concepts, Mouse and Icons
questions.explanation: Keyboard shortcuts speed up common tasks.

questions.question: The Windows program used to view, copy, move and organise files and folders is:
questions.subject: Windows Concepts, Mouse and Icons
questions.explanation: It can be opened with Windows key + E.

questions.question: To select several files that are NOT next to each other in File Explorer, the user holds down:
questions.subject: Windows Concepts, Mouse and Icons
questions.explanation: Shift + click selects a continuous range of items.

questions.question: The mouse pointer changes to a spinning circle (or hourglass in older Windows) when:

options.D: The computer is busy and the user should wait

questions.subject: Windows Concepts, Mouse and Icons
questions.explanation: An I-beam pointer appears over text that can be edited.

questions.question: Dragging a file with the RIGHT mouse button and releasing it shows a menu with options such as:

options.A: Copy here, Move here and Create shortcuts here

questions.subject: Windows Concepts, Mouse and Icons
questions.explanation: It lets the user choose exactly what should happen.

questions.question: The main screen that appears after logging in to Windows, with icons and the taskbar, is called the:
questions.subject: Windows Concepts, Mouse and Icons
questions.explanation: Windows are opened on top of the desktop.

questions.question:
Consider the statements:
I. A folder can contain files and other folders.
II. Deleting a shortcut icon also deletes the original program.
Which is/are correct?
questions.subject: Windows Concepts, Mouse and Icons
questions.explanation: A shortcut is only a link to the original item.

questions.question:
Consider the statements:
I. Double-clicking an icon normally opens the item it represents.
II. Right-clicking an item normally shows a context menu of actions for that item.
Which is/are correct?
questions.subject: Windows Concepts, Mouse and Icons
questions.explanation: Both are standard mouse actions in Windows.

questions.question:
Assertion (A): A file deleted with the Delete key can usually be recovered in Windows.
Reason (R): Such files are first moved to the Recycle Bin.

options.A: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
options.B: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
options.C: A is true, but R is false
options.D: A is false, but R is true

questions.subject: Windows Concepts, Mouse and Icons
questions.explanation: Files can be restored from the Recycle Bin until it is emptied.

questions.question:
Assertion (A): Minimising a window closes the program.
Reason (R): A minimised window remains available as a button on the taskbar.

options.A: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
options.B: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
options.C: A is true, but R is false
options.D: A is false, but R is true

questions.subject: Windows Concepts, Mouse and Icons
questions.explanation: The program keeps running on the taskbar, which shows why A is false.

questions.question: In Windows, the Control Panel is used mainly to:

options.D: View and change system settings such as hardware, programs, users and appearance

questions.subject: Control Panel and Personalisation
questions.explanation: In Windows 10/11 many of these settings have moved to the Settings app.

questions.question: Which keyboard shortcut opens the Settings app in Windows 10/11?
questions.subject: Control Panel and Personalisation
questions.explanation: Win + E opens File Explorer.

questions.question: To uninstall a program using the Control Panel, you go to:
questions.subject: Control Panel and Personalisation
questions.explanation: In Settings it is Apps → Installed apps.

questions.question: The picture displayed as the background of the Windows desktop is called the:
questions.subject: Control Panel and Personalisation
questions.explanation: It is changed under Personalization → Background.

questions.question: A moving picture or pattern that appears when the computer is idle for a set time is a:
questions.subject: Control Panel and Personalisation
questions.explanation: It was originally used to prevent image burn-in on CRT monitors.

questions.question: A Windows 'theme' is:

options.C: A combination of desktop background, colours, sounds and mouse cursor

questions.subject: Control Panel and Personalisation
questions.explanation: Applying a theme changes several appearance settings at once.

questions.question: Changing screen resolution in Windows is done from:
questions.subject: Control Panel and Personalisation
questions.explanation: Right-clicking the desktop and choosing Display settings also opens it.

questions.question: A higher screen resolution (e.g. 1920 × 1080 instead of 1366 × 768) means:

options.A: More pixels, so items look smaller and sharper and more fits on screen

questions.subject: Control Panel and Personalisation
questions.explanation: Resolution is the number of pixels horizontally × vertically.

questions.question: Which Control Panel/Settings category is used to set the system date, time and time zone?

options.D: Clock and Region (Time & language in Settings)

questions.subject: Control Panel and Personalisation
questions.explanation: Region settings also control date and number formats.

questions.question: Ease of Access (Accessibility) settings include:
questions.subject: Control Panel and Personalisation
questions.explanation: They help users with visual, hearing or motor difficulties.

questions.question: The Windows tool that reads aloud text on the screen for visually impaired users is:
questions.subject: Control Panel and Personalisation
questions.explanation: Magnifier enlarges part of the screen.

questions.question: To add a new user account on a Windows PC, you use:

options.A: User Accounts in Control Panel / Accounts in Settings

questions.subject: Control Panel and Personalisation
questions.explanation: Accounts can be standard users or administrators.

questions.question: Device Manager in Windows is used to:

options.D: View hardware devices and update, disable or uninstall their drivers

questions.subject: Control Panel and Personalisation
questions.explanation: A yellow warning sign marks a device with a problem.

questions.question: Mouse settings in Control Panel allow you to:

options.A: Swap primary and secondary buttons and change pointer speed and double-click speed

questions.subject: Control Panel and Personalisation
questions.explanation: Left-handed users often swap the buttons.

questions.question: Which setting controls how long the computer waits before turning off the display or sleeping?
questions.subject: Control Panel and Personalisation
questions.explanation: It is found under System in Settings or Hardware and Sound in Control Panel.

questions.question:
Match the Windows item with its purpose:
a. Device Manager
b. Narrator
c. Programs and Features
d. Personalization

1. Managing hardware drivers
2. Changing background, colours and themes
3. Uninstalling software
4. Reading screen text aloud
questions.subject: Control Panel and Personalisation
questions.explanation: Each is found through Control Panel or Settings.

questions.question:
Consider the statements:
I. The screen saver and the desktop background are the same thing.
II. Screen resolution can be changed in Display settings.
Which is/are correct?
questions.subject: Control Panel and Personalisation
questions.explanation: The background is always visible behind windows; the screen saver appears only when the PC is idle.

questions.question:
Consider the statements:
I. Windows lets you change the mouse pointer size and colour.
II. Windows lets left-handed users swap the mouse buttons.
Which is/are correct?
questions.subject: Control Panel and Personalisation
questions.explanation: Both are available in mouse and accessibility settings.

questions.question:
Assertion (A): The Control Panel lets a user uninstall programs.
Reason (R): Programs and Features lists the installed software with an Uninstall option.

options.A: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
options.B: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
options.C: A is true, but R is false
options.D: A is false, but R is true

questions.subject: Control Panel and Personalisation
questions.explanation: That is where uninstallation is done.

questions.question:
Assertion (A): A higher screen resolution makes icons appear larger.
Reason (R): Resolution is the number of pixels displayed on the screen.

options.A: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
options.B: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
options.C: A is true, but R is false
options.D: A is false, but R is true

questions.subject: Control Panel and Personalisation
questions.explanation: More pixels make each item smaller on the same screen; A is false.

questions.question: Right-clicking an item in Windows usually opens a:

options.B: New window of the Control Panel
options.D: Context (shortcut) menu with actions for that item

questions.subject: Menus, Toolbars, Right-click and Shortcuts
questions.explanation: The options depend on what was right-clicked.

questions.question: The keyboard shortcut to copy selected items is:
questions.subject: Menus, Toolbars, Right-click and Shortcuts
questions.explanation: Ctrl + X cuts and Ctrl + V pastes.

questions.question: The keyboard shortcut to undo the last action is:
questions.subject: Menus, Toolbars, Right-click and Shortcuts
questions.explanation: Ctrl + Y usually redoes.

questions.question: Alt + Tab is used to:
questions.subject: Menus, Toolbars, Right-click and Shortcuts
questions.explanation: Keep Alt held and press Tab repeatedly to move through windows.

questions.question: Alt + F4 is used to:

options.D: Close the active window (or shut down when on the desktop)

questions.subject: Menus, Toolbars, Right-click and Shortcuts
questions.explanation: On the desktop it opens the Shut Down Windows dialog.

questions.question: Which shortcut opens Task Manager directly?
questions.subject: Menus, Toolbars, Right-click and Shortcuts
questions.explanation: Ctrl + Alt + Del opens a screen that includes Task Manager.

questions.question: Windows key + D is used to:
questions.subject: Menus, Toolbars, Right-click and Shortcuts
questions.explanation: Win + L locks the computer.

questions.question: Windows key + L is used to:

options.C: Log off permanently and delete files

questions.subject: Menus, Toolbars, Right-click and Shortcuts
questions.explanation: It protects the PC when you step away.

questions.question: Windows key + R opens:
questions.subject: Menus, Toolbars, Right-click and Shortcuts
questions.explanation: You can type commands such as 'notepad' or 'control' there.

questions.question: The F2 key, with a file selected in File Explorer, is used to:
questions.subject: Menus, Toolbars, Right-click and Shortcuts
questions.explanation: F5 refreshes; F1 opens Help.

questions.question: Shift + Delete on a file in Windows:

options.B: Moves it to the Recycle Bin
options.C: Deletes it permanently without sending it to the Recycle Bin

questions.subject: Menus, Toolbars, Right-click and Shortcuts
questions.explanation: Windows asks for confirmation first.

questions.question: The bar at the bottom of the Windows screen showing the Start button, pinned and open programs is the:
questions.subject: Menus, Toolbars, Right-click and Shortcuts
questions.explanation: The notification area (system tray) is at its right end.

questions.question: The bar at the top of a window that shows its name and the Minimise, Maximise and Close buttons is the:
questions.subject: Menus, Toolbars, Right-click and Shortcuts
questions.explanation: Double-clicking it maximises or restores the window.

questions.question: A toolbar in an application is:

options.C: A row of buttons or icons giving quick access to commonly used commands
options.D: A list of files on disk

questions.subject: Menus, Toolbars, Right-click and Shortcuts
questions.explanation: The Quick Access Toolbar in MS Office is an example.

questions.question: A menu item followed by three dots (…), such as 'Save As…', means that choosing it will:

options.D: Open a dialog box asking for more information

questions.subject: Menus, Toolbars, Right-click and Shortcuts
questions.explanation: A small arrow (▶) indicates a submenu.

questions.question: Snapping a window to the left half of the screen can be done with:
questions.subject: Menus, Toolbars, Right-click and Shortcuts
questions.explanation: Windows 11 also offers Snap layouts with Win + Z.

questions.question:
Match the shortcut with its action:
a. Ctrl + A
b. Ctrl + X
c. Win + E
d. Ctrl + Shift + Esc

1. Cut
2. Select all
3. Open Task Manager
4. Open File Explorer
questions.subject: Menus, Toolbars, Right-click and Shortcuts
questions.explanation: These are standard Windows shortcuts.

questions.question:
Consider the statements:
I. Shift + Delete sends a file to the Recycle Bin.
II. Ctrl + V pastes the contents of the clipboard.
Which is/are correct?
questions.subject: Menus, Toolbars, Right-click and Shortcuts
questions.explanation: Shift + Delete bypasses the Recycle Bin.

questions.question:
Assertion (A): Keyboard shortcuts can make work faster.
Reason (R): They perform commands without navigating through menus with the mouse.

options.A: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
options.B: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
options.C: A is true, but R is false
options.D: A is false, but R is true

questions.subject: Menus, Toolbars, Right-click and Shortcuts
questions.explanation: That is their purpose.

questions.question:
Assertion (A): Win + L locks the computer.
Reason (R): Win + D closes all open programs permanently.

options.A: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
options.B: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
options.C: A is true, but R is false
options.D: A is false, but R is true

questions.subject: Menus, Toolbars, Right-click and Shortcuts
questions.explanation: A is true; R is false – Win + D only shows the desktop; programs keep running.

sets.name: 1 · Document Setting, Page Layout and Save Options

questions.question: The default file extension of a document saved in Word 2007 and later versions is:
questions.subject: Document Setting, Page Layout and Save Options
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KPSC / KEA / SSC). Word 97–2003 used .doc; .docx is an XML-based format.

questions.question: A Word template file (without macros) has the extension:
questions.subject: Document Setting, Page Layout and Save Options
questions.explanation: Templates give a ready-made layout for new documents.

questions.question: Which key opens the 'Save As' dialog box in Word?
questions.subject: Document Setting, Page Layout and Save Options
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KPSC / KEA / SSC). F7 checks spelling, F5 opens Go To, F1 opens Help.

questions.question: The difference between Save and Save As is that Save As:

options.A: Lets you save the document with a new name, location or format

questions.subject: Document Setting, Page Layout and Save Options
questions.explanation: Save simply updates the existing file.

questions.question: Page orientation (portrait or landscape) is changed from the:
questions.subject: Document Setting, Page Layout and Save Options
questions.explanation: Older versions call it the Page Layout tab.

questions.question: A document page wider than it is tall has:
questions.subject: Document Setting, Page Layout and Save Options
questions.explanation: Portrait is taller than it is wide.

questions.question: The standard A4 paper size is:
questions.subject: Document Setting, Page Layout and Save Options
questions.explanation: 8.5 × 11 inches is US Letter; 297 × 420 mm is A3.

questions.question: The blank space between the text and the edges of a page is called the:
questions.subject: Document Setting, Page Layout and Save Options
questions.explanation: Margins are set under Layout → Margins.

questions.question: Text that appears at the top of every page, such as a document title, is placed in the:
questions.subject: Document Setting, Page Layout and Save Options
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KPSC / KEA / SSC). The footer is at the bottom; both are inserted from the Insert tab.

questions.question: Which keyboard shortcut inserts a manual page break in Word?
questions.subject: Document Setting, Page Layout and Save Options
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KPSC / KEA / SSC). Shift + Enter inserts a line break within the same paragraph.

questions.question: To show text in newspaper-style side-by-side columns, you use:
questions.subject: Document Setting, Page Layout and Save Options
questions.explanation: Column breaks can be added from Layout → Breaks.

questions.question: Faint text such as 'CONFIDENTIAL' behind the main text on every page is a:
questions.subject: Document Setting, Page Layout and Save Options
questions.explanation: It is added from the Design tab (Page Layout in older versions).

questions.question: Which Word feature creates personalised letters for many recipients from one main document and a data list?
questions.subject: Document Setting, Page Layout and Save Options
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KPSC / KEA / SSC). It is on the Mailings tab.

questions.question: Word can save a document directly in which format for sharing without allowing easy editing?
questions.subject: Document Setting, Page Layout and Save Options
questions.explanation: Use File → Save As and choose PDF.

questions.question: AutoRecover in Word:

options.B: Periodically saves recovery information so work can be restored after a crash

questions.subject: Document Setting, Page Layout and Save Options
questions.explanation: The interval is set in File → Options → Save.

questions.question: Line spacing of a paragraph is changed from the:

options.A: Paragraph group of the Home tab

questions.subject: Document Setting, Page Layout and Save Options
questions.explanation: Common values are 1.0, 1.15, 1.5 and 2.0.

questions.question:
Match the Word tab with a command found on it:
a. Insert
b. Layout
c. Mailings
d. Review

1. Header
2. Track Changes
3. Start Mail Merge
4. Margins
questions.subject: Document Setting, Page Layout and Save Options
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KPSC / KEA / SSC). Knowing where commands live on the Ribbon is often tested.

questions.question:
Consider the statements:
I. Portrait orientation is taller than it is wide.
II. Headers appear at the bottom of each page.
Which is/are correct?
questions.subject: Document Setting, Page Layout and Save Options
questions.explanation: Footers appear at the bottom.

questions.question:
Assertion (A): Save As can be used to keep the original file unchanged while saving an edited copy.
Reason (R): Save As saves the document under a new name or location.

options.A: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
options.B: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
options.C: A is true, but R is false
options.D: A is false, but R is true

questions.subject: Document Setting, Page Layout and Save Options
questions.explanation: The original file remains as it was last saved.

questions.question:
Assertion (A): Shift + Enter starts a new page.
Reason (R): Ctrl + Enter inserts a page break.

options.A: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
options.B: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
options.C: A is true, but R is false
options.D: A is false, but R is true

questions.subject: Document Setting, Page Layout and Save Options
questions.explanation: Shift + Enter inserts a line break; A is false, R is true.

questions.question: In Word 2007 and later, the menus and toolbars of older versions were replaced by the:
questions.subject: Editing, Toolbars, Sorting and Shortcuts
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KPSC / KEA / SSC). The Ribbon groups commands into tabs such as Home, Insert and Layout.

questions.question: The small customisable toolbar above or below the Ribbon, holding commands such as Save and Undo, is the:
questions.subject: Editing, Toolbars, Sorting and Shortcuts
questions.explanation: You can add your most-used commands to it.

questions.question: Which shortcut makes selected text bold?
questions.subject: Editing, Toolbars, Sorting and Shortcuts
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KPSC / KEA / SSC). Ctrl + I = italic, Ctrl + U = underline; Ctrl + D opens the Font dialog.

questions.question: Which shortcut centres the selected paragraph?
questions.subject: Editing, Toolbars, Sorting and Shortcuts
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KPSC / KEA / SSC). Ctrl + L left, Ctrl + R right, Ctrl + J justify.

questions.question: Ctrl + J applies which alignment?
questions.subject: Editing, Toolbars, Sorting and Shortcuts
questions.explanation: Justified text has straight edges on both sides.

questions.question: Which shortcut opens Find and Replace with the Replace tab selected?
questions.subject: Editing, Toolbars, Sorting and Shortcuts
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KPSC / KEA / SSC). Ctrl + F opens Find (Navigation pane); Ctrl + G opens Go To.

questions.question: Which key starts the spelling and grammar check in Word?
questions.subject: Editing, Toolbars, Sorting and Shortcuts
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KPSC / KEA / SSC). Shift + F7 opens the Thesaurus.

questions.question: Shift + F7 in Word opens the:
questions.subject: Editing, Toolbars, Sorting and Shortcuts
questions.explanation: It suggests synonyms for the selected word.

questions.question: Which shortcut redoes (or repeats) the last action?
questions.subject: Editing, Toolbars, Sorting and Shortcuts
questions.explanation: Ctrl + Z undoes it.

questions.question: Ctrl + Home moves the cursor to the:
questions.subject: Editing, Toolbars, Sorting and Shortcuts
questions.explanation: Ctrl + End moves to the end of the document; Home alone goes to the start of the line.

questions.question: The Format Painter tool is used to:

options.A: Copy formatting from one piece of text and apply it to another

questions.subject: Editing, Toolbars, Sorting and Shortcuts
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KPSC / KEA / SSC). Double-click it to apply the format to several places.

questions.question: The Office Clipboard in Word can hold up to how many copied items?
questions.subject: Editing, Toolbars, Sorting and Shortcuts
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KPSC / KEA / SSC). The Windows clipboard alone holds only the last item (without clipboard history).

questions.question: To arrange a list of names in alphabetical order in Word, you use:
questions.subject: Editing, Toolbars, Sorting and Shortcuts
questions.explanation: Sort can order text, numbers or dates, ascending or descending.

questions.question: Which shortcut makes the selected text superscript (as in x²)?
questions.subject: Editing, Toolbars, Sorting and Shortcuts
questions.explanation: Ctrl + = makes subscript (as in H₂O).

questions.question: Ctrl + Shift + > applied to selected text:

options.C: Moves it to the next page

questions.subject: Editing, Toolbars, Sorting and Shortcuts
questions.explanation: Ctrl + Shift + < decreases the font size.

questions.question: Track Changes, used when several people edit a document, is found on the:
questions.subject: Editing, Toolbars, Sorting and Shortcuts
questions.explanation: Each change can later be accepted or rejected.

questions.question:
Match the shortcut with its action in Word:
a. Ctrl + L
b. Ctrl + U
c. Ctrl + P
d. Ctrl + N

1. New document
2. Underline
3. Align left
4. Print
questions.subject: Editing, Toolbars, Sorting and Shortcuts
questions.explanation: PYQ pattern (KPSC / KEA / SSC). A frequent matching question.

questions.question:
Consider the statements:
I. Ctrl + F opens Find in Word.
II. Ctrl + H opens the Replace tab of Find and Replace.
Which is/are correct?
questions.subject: Editing, Toolbars, Sorting and Shortcuts
questions.explanation: Both are correct.

questions.question:
Assertion (A): Format Painter saves time when formatting documents.
Reason (R): It copies formatting, not text, from one place to another.

options.A: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
options.B: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
options.C: A is true, but R is false
options.D: A is false, but R is true

questions.subject: Editing, Toolbars, Sorting and Shortcuts
questions.explanation: Only the look is transferred.

questions.question:
Assertion (A): F7 opens the Thesaurus in Word.
Reason (R): Word can check spelling and grammar.

options.A: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
options.B: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
options.C: A is true, but R is false
options.D: A is false, but R is true

questions.subject: Editing, Toolbars, Sorting and Shortcuts
questions.explanation: F7 starts the spelling and grammar check; Shift + F7 opens the Thesaurus. A is false, R is true.
